title: no license required....to drive or travel.....supreme court ruling.in alot of cases over the years .
summary: Reading of a list of right-to-travel case citations claiming no license, registration or insurance is needed to drive.

assertions.quote: u.s supreme court says no license necessary to drive an automobile

verdicts.note: The court cites its own and other courts' repeated rejection of right-to-travel-without-a-license arguments. The rulings run the other way.

assertions.quote: travel is not a privilege requiring license and vehicle registration or forced insurance

verdicts.note: The court holds the right to travel is not a right to drive: driving is a regulable privilege, and the licensing statute leaves a person free to travel by other means; convictions for no license affirmed.
The Supreme Court upheld conviction of a man driving his own car from his office into Maryland without the required registration; licensing private drivers is valid police power.

Driving unlicensed as 'travelling' is called an illegal OPCA activity based on a spurious driving/travelling distinction, comprehensively rejected in d'Abadie (Alberta); a Canadian trial-level ruling on a common-law version, not a US constitutional holding.

assertions.quote: merely traveling without compensation or profit outside of a business enterprise or adventure with the corporate state no license is required

verdicts.note: A driver with a homemade 'private' plate who claimed a right to travel privately without a license was convicted of license and plate offenses, affirmed on appeal.

A litigant ticketed for driving without licence, insurance and registration under a 'private non commercial use only' plate was rebuffed and declared vexatious; the driving/travelling distinction is called spurious and was comprehensively rejected.

assertions.quote: refusal to answer furnishes no basis for an arrest
may ignore the law engage with impunity and exercise of such right

verdicts.note: Shuttlesworth allows ignoring a facially unconstitutional, standardless speech permit, but it does not reach driver licensing.
Licensing does not unlawfully restrict the right to travel; the defendant who ignored it was convicted and the convictions were affirmed.

assertions.quote: traffic infractions are not a crime

verdicts.note: Many states classify minor traffic violations as civil infractions, but driving unlicensed or unregistered is often a misdemeanor.

In Ohio, failure to display a license is an unclassified misdemeanor and a missing plate is a minor misdemeanor, criminal offenses; some states treat infractions as civil, so the blanket claim fails here.

assertions.quote: the right to travel freely from state to state is a right broadly assertable against private interference as well as government action

verdicts.note: Shapiro v. Thompson and Saenz v. Roe recognise a right of interstate migration, which does not include driving unlicensed.
The Court recognizes, per Crandall v. Nevada, a right of US citizens to pass through the states that a direct exit tax would violate, while upholding licensing.
